### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via translatePage (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 62bc1293080968f0ec8c3d31dc1f9ed8da4077df` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0d27c0cd444658440ed5b67317ae6be68aefd048` — the merge of head `f18a2f55dd050513dc8fe2dfdfab4217b5f48dff` into base `62bc1293080968f0ec8c3d31dc1f9ed8da4077df`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0d27c0cd444658440ed5b67317ae6be68aefd048 && git checkout 0d27c0cd444658440ed5b67317ae6be68aefd048
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 62bc1293080968f0ec8c3d31dc1f9ed8da4077df f18a2f55dd050513dc8fe2dfdfab4217b5f48dff && git checkout -B drift-repro 62bc1293080968f0ec8c3d31dc1f9ed8da4077df && git merge --no-ff f18a2f55dd050513dc8fe2dfdfab4217b5f48dff

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 62bc1293080968f0ec8c3d31dc1f9ed8da4077df
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 62bc1293080968f0ec8c3d31dc1f9ed8da4077df` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f18a2f55dd050513dc8fe2dfdfab4217b5f48dff`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/system.json, packages/spec/export-origins/system.json, .changeset/24968-page-tabs-item-label-key.md, content/docs/ui/translations.mdx

Read against card #24968 (body, claim 6300704588, correction 6300738468, dev reports 6304394234 and 6307292111), the standing ruling on #6015 (comment 6292005854, rule 甲), the PR body and file list, and the three-dot diff `origin/main...f18a2f55dd`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Delta from the previously reviewed head `c8a248af73`** (the two three-dot diffs against `origin/main` compared line by line, so the `origin/main` merge `7e29242308` cancels out): one commit, `f18a2f55dd`. It drops the `tabs` to `items` alias from the page component entry's alias table (the `view-list-tabs-retirement` pin read the literal `tabs` key in that object as a retired ListView payload), drops the one schema test and the one changeset sentence that named it, and adds the `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` table row this review had flagged. Nothing else differs: resolver, walk, lint, extractor, exports, generated artifacts and every other test are byte-identical to the previous head. The alias was an error-message hint on a key the strictObject refused on `main` and still refuses, so its removal changes no accept set; the head is narrower than what was reviewed before only in its guidance prose, and remains a pure widening against `main`. Every judgment below was re-read against the new head and holds.

### ① Derived judgments

- **New key `pages.PAGE.components.TABS_ID.items.VALUE.label` (translation.zod.ts).** On `main` the component entry is a `strictObject` over `title`/`description`/`label`/`placeholder`/`emptyText`, so `items` (and `tabs`) under `components.ID` was refused as an unknown key. The head declares `items` as a record of closed entries (surface "this page tab item translation", one key `label`, aliases `name`/`title`/`text` to `label`); the component entry's own alias table is unchanged from `main`. Every input that parsed on `main` still parses; a previously refused input now parses. Widening. The "declares exactly the keys the resolver and the extractor act on" pin still holds because `items` is optional and absent from that parse. The item key carries the same `I18nLabelSchema` caveat as the component copy: the bundle entry wins, an unkeyed item keeps its inline map (pinned by the resolver test).
- **Identity choice (shape a).** `PageTabsProps.items[].value` is optional and the renderer falls back to `tab-` plus the index (component.zod.ts, read point recorded in `liveness/page.json`); the extractor header already records the #14749 direction "identity first: component.id / section.name / tabs item.value". Keying by `value` under the tabs component id adds no authorable key to a published page schema and no second identifier per tab. An item without a `value` has no key, consistent with the array-index prohibition. `page:accordion` is excluded for a documented reason: its item `value` is refused with guidance because the renderer overwrites it with `panel-INDEX`. Accepted. Nit, not blocking: nothing in the schema or lint refuses two items in one strip sharing a `value`; both would then receive the same translation, which is also what the renderer's `?tab=` token already does for them.
- **`translatePage` (i18n-resolver.ts).** `translatePageTabItems` runs under the same `addressed` arbitration as the component copy, only for `component.type === PAGE_TABS_COMPONENT_TYPE`, before the `if (nested) return next` cut, so nested tabs components are reached by the id route. The lookup walks the locale chain per item and writes only where the bundle has a non-empty string, returning the component untouched otherwise. No existing key's resolution changes.
- **`walkAddressedPageComponents`.** On `main` a panel list was rebuilt from the authored entry (`{...entry, [panelKey]: visitedChildren}`), and the docblock stated that a visitor's edit to a panel's own key is overwritten. The head spreads `own[i]` instead, where `own` is the visitor's returned list only when it keeps the authored shape (same length, a plain object at every authored panel position), else the authored list; `[panelKey]` is still the authored panel's children, visited. For a visitor that returns the component unchanged or re-spreads it with the same `items` array (the extractor, lint's new universe pass, objectui's validator, and `translatePage` before this change), `own === list` and the output is byte-for-byte what `main` produced. Behaviour differs only for a visitor that already edited panel keys, whose edits were previously discarded by contract and now stand. Descent order, depth cap, cycle guard, root-level collision arbitration, the two-positions-one-key compose path (`rebuilt[key]` reused on the second position) and the "no panel in the list, no rebuild" rule are unchanged. Signature and return shape unchanged. Widening of the visitor contract, pinned by a new walk test. Note the docblock change is itself a contract statement a downstream visitor may now rely on; it is consistent with the code.
- **Lint refusals (validate-translation-references.ts).** The three `translation-target-unknown` arms (unknown `value` including an index token, `items` on a non-tabs component with the accordion given the inline-map remedy, `items` under an undeclared component id) judge only the `items` member. Under 甲 the question is whether any of them refuses something that passes today: no. On `main`, `items` under `components.ID` fails `TranslationDataSchema` as an unknown key before any reference check runs, so no bundle that validates today carries the member these arms read. They narrow nothing; they are the reference check for a key that did not exist. Severity `error` is correct. The universe is built on spec's `walkAddressedPageComponents`, the walk the reader runs, so the ids and item values lint accepts are the ones the resolver applies; sibling-package pages are collected with the existing `ownDeclaration` precedence. Pages the stack does not declare are skipped, consistent with the rest of the rule (acceptance note 1).
- **Extractor slot and coverage demand (i18n-extract.ts, i18n-coverage.ts).** `emitPageComponentCopy` emits one slot per valued item of an addressed `page:tabs`, through the same `pushEntry` path as component copy, so an inline locale map on the label is recorded as `inlineLocales` and coverage treats it as authored for the locales it covers (pinned). Because a reader exists, the slot is demanded, which is the inverse of #24943 and the right side of that line. Consequence for an existing downstream app: a `page:tabs` with valued items and no inline map now shows the tab labels as missing in `check:i18n-coverage` for each non-source locale. That is the measured defect itself (HotCRM's three English tabs) becoming visible to the gate the card asked to see it, and the remedy is the scaffold `os i18n extract` writes; an app already localizing by inline map stays green. Acceptable. In-repo, the dev reports `check:i18n-coverage` at 14 configs with none new and exit 0; CI's Test Core runs are the record of that on this head.
- **New exports `PAGE_TABS_COMPONENT_TYPE`, `pageTabItemKey`.** Exported from `i18n-resolver.ts` through `system/index.ts` (`export *`), recorded in `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json`. Additive. `pageTabItemKey` is total over `unknown` and returns `undefined` for a non-object, an array, a missing, non-string or empty `value`; the resolver, extractor and lint all address an item through it, which is the drift guard the PR claims.
- **Generated artifacts.** The strictness-ledger counts (`docs/audits/.../system.md`) move by one closed entry; the reference `translation.mdx` is unchanged because its `components` cell is truncated. Consistent with the diff.

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/cli` (all three published at 18.0.0), with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset. Matches what publishes: a new accepted key and two new exports in spec, a new refusal arm in lint over a key that was previously unparseable, a new extractor slot in the CLI. No existing accepted input is refused, no existing resolution changes, no signature or return shape changes. No ADR-0087 conversion is owed because nothing authored is rewritten. `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green on the head. Agreed: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev out-of-scope 1** (lint judges no other `pages.PAGE` member: unknown page name, unknown component id carrying only copy keys): confirmed as pre-existing on `main` and untouched here. Not blocking; left as recorded, no card owed by this review.
- **Dev out-of-scope 2** (`page:accordion` panel labels have no bundle key): confirmed against `component.zod.ts`, where the accordion item `value` is refused because the renderer derives `panel-INDEX`. Deliberate and documented in the new schema docblock and the lint verdict. Not blocking.
- **Hand-written docs.** Resolved at `f18a2f55dd`: `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` gains a "Page tab labels (`page:tabs` items)" row naming the key, the `value` identity, the no-`value` case and the accordion exclusion. It matches the schema docblock and the lint verdicts.
- **PR body.** The seat patched the Spec bullet to say the `tabs` alias was dropped in `f18a2f55dd`; the body, the changeset and the committed schema now agree.
- **Overlap with #24947** (same seat, `i18n-extract.ts`): the head's hunk is inside `emitPageComponentCopy`; the dev reports #24947 edits a different function. Merge-order risk only, no contract question.
- **`wip:` commit `818b89e351` in the branch history.** The PR squash-lands; the net three-dot diff is what was reviewed. No flag.
- **Check-runs.** On `f18a2f55dd` at the time of this review every completed check-run is success or skipped: Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core and its six shards, the four Type Check jobs, every Lint job, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate and the card-claim guards; none is red. Two re-triggered runs (Check Changeset, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path) were still in progress at that reading, each with an earlier successful completion on the same head. The seat posts this record once every run on the head has completed. Nothing was re-run locally.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24968-page-tabs-item-label-key`
Reviewed-by: `session_01D6F9axfoPzR7t8G1J7Ytzz`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**Seat re-read of the check-runs at landing:** all 49 runs on `f18a2f55dd` have completed: 41 succeeded, the rest were skipped, and none is red.
